summary_paragraph: A 59-year-old woman with HIV/AIDS and end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis was admitted for pleuritic chest pain. Initial workup ruled out cardiac, pulmonary, and aortic causes. The pain resolved with Percocet and was attributed to gastritis and chronic musculoskeletal discomfort. She developed coagulase-negative staphylococcal bacteremia, likely from her dialysis line, prompting line removal and placement of a temporary right groin catheter. Vancomycin was administered for 10 days via dialysis. She also had transient fevers with a retrocardiac opacity on X-ray, which resolved without further intervention. Gastritis was treated with omeprazole, and prophylactic Bactrim and azithromycin were restarted. The patient was discharged home with plans for follow-up in nephrology, infectious disease, and neurology, and education on medication changes, particularly the need to switch from omeprazole when restarting antiretroviral therapy.
